newsitem.title: CHINA: China says rail income rises, traffic dips.
newsitem.headline: China says rail income rises, traffic dips.

text.p: China's railways showed higher passenger and freight earnings in the second quarter despite a drop in overall traffic as many less profitable services were halted, the China Daily said on Monday.
The rise in profits accompanied a programme to boost train speed, starting in April, the newspaper said, adding that ticket prices had not been increased over the period.
Railway earnings were up 6.0 percent year-on-year in June after a rise of 2.3 percent in May and 1.7 percent in April, it said without giving total figures.
"We are pleased to see that railways are making more profit both in the passenger and cargo sectors now," Chang Guozhi, an official of the Railways Ministry, was quoted as saying.
The railways -- once the backbone of the domestic transport system -- have been struggling to compete with rivals such as long distance buses and airlines as roads and air service improve.

Rail passenger traffic in the second quarter fell 6.2 percent from a year ago and the number of trains in service was reduced by 11 percent amid the discontinuation of service on many low-speed, short-distance routes, the China Daily said.
Since April 1, train speed had been raised on three major lines linking the capital with the southern city of Guangzhou, the commercial centre of Shanghai and the northeastern city of Harbin.
It said 64 direct express or overnight train routes had been inaugurated during the period and the load factor on such services had risen to over 95 percent from 40-60 percent in the first quarter.
